lead: GameStop / GME — is the meme stock back?
smaller: Dogecoin / DOGE — ready to run again?
IonQ / IONQ — Jensen Huang cooled quantum, so buy the dip
Tesla / TSLA — Musk is back in charge
why_lead: GameStop had the strongest price evidence among the crowd's names in the prior session, with GME up 11.65% that day and up 19.61% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-26).
The attention is aligned with the move: the bitcoin-treasury plan is being covered as a meme-stock revival, and the same-day Q4 beat gives the story a business cover [[n0548]] [[n6329]].
The story is simple enough for the crowd to repeat, and it coincides with bitcoin proxies moving with it (MSTR up 25.08% over 20 sessions).
why_smaller: Dogecoin is the non-equity trade, with DOGE up 16.60% over five sessions and retail sentiment bullish on the adjacent coins, while the 20-session base is still negative.
Quantum is the dip-buying narrative, with IONQ down 17.14% over 20 sessions after Nvidia's CEO tempered quantum expectations, and a director buying shares.
Tesla is the Musk-comeback narrative, distinct from the bitcoin and meme story, with a five-session gain of 15.35% against a 20-session loss of 6.44%.
considered_not_chosen: Tesla as the lead: a five-session gain of 15.35% and a Musk all-hands story, but the prior session fell 5.58% and the same-day coverage centred on European sales and tariff concerns, so price and attention did not coincide as cleanly as GameStop's; it is used as a smaller trade.

Rheinmetall and European defence: the largest 20-session gain in the card (up 39.54%), but the attention is institutional (a new defence ETF, supplier coverage) rather than retail; used in underowned and in the auto sector block.
Copper: a record US price on tariff bets and a 20-session gain of 14.84%, but no retail-attention cluster in the window; used in the materials block and underowned themes.
CoreWeave IPO interest and Nebius: the IPO has retail interest but no price in the card, and Nebius's 31.32% 20-session drawdown has no same-window attention story to pair with it.
Robinhood: down 8.43% over 20 sessions, but the attention is product news (banking, prediction markets), not the trade itself.
Leveraged ETFs (TQQQ down 18.87%, SOXL down 28.53% over 20 sessions): a clear drawdown, but the attention is a regulatory item in Thailand rather than crowd buying.
Palantir: widely-held lists and a 20-session gain of only 3.33%, so no surge to pair with the attention.
Oklo and nuclear: a 25.06% 20-session drawdown and a design milestone; used in the catalysts block rather than in the retail section.
eToro: IPO filing attention with no price in the card.
